physical.title: flag
physical.summary: Asafo flag with an elephant and palm tree. Basecloth made of yellow silk with rectangles of blue silk in the corners; black cotton border sewn along one side, and red, yellow, blue and white triangles appliquéd around other three sides. Lettered in light blue cursive characters ‘No.III Company Anamaboe’. The central design is an elephant embroidered in brown silk with its trunk round a palm tree, with another tree bent over next to it. In an upper corner is a Union Jack.

physical.title: flag
physical.summary: Asafo flag with two headless corpses. The base cloth is of imported green and red silk damask. Base cloth of green and red floral damask, which is edged on three sides with alternating red and white cotton squares, plus a white cotton fringe. There is a wide strip with cotton ties on the fourth side. The central design on both sides shows two soldiers, one in red and one in black holding a red sword; at their feet lie two heads cut from corpses which lie beside them in white. A version of the Union Jack in red and white cotton has been sewn down onto an upper corner.

physical.title: flag
physical.summary: Asafo flag, with a man and woman. The base cloth is built up of yellow cotton and green silk rectangles, edged by white rectangles alternating with red squares and with a white cotton fringe; there is a wide strip with cotton ties on the fourth side. The central design on both sides shows a man playing a drum, with a woman in front holding out her hands (both in black cotton) and a snake (in blue cotton) behind her. The features of the two figures and the snake have been embroidered in cotton thread. A Union Jack in red, white and blue cotton has been sewn down onto an upper corner.

physical.title: flag
physical.summary: Asafo flag with a central chequerboard pattern (there are no figurative elements) of white and blue squares of silk; this is edged on three sides by rectangles of white cotton and red and blue silk which terminate in a fringe of cut white cotton. The fourth side has a wide band of white cotton with ties. In the upper corner, where a Union Jack is often placed, is a pattern of red, blue and white triangles which may signify the Dutch flag.
